rules.rule: A promissory note is a signed written unconditional undertaking by its maker to pay a certain sum of money to a certain person, their order or bearer, on demand or at a fixed or determinable future time.
rules.plain_language: It is a promise to pay made by the note's maker.
rules.scenario_relevance: The project says a note relating to credit-bought stock falls due. The note itself and its maturity terms are not supplied.

rules.rule: A bill of exchange is a signed written unconditional order directing a certain person to pay a certain sum to a certain person, their order or bearer, on demand or at a fixed or determinable future time.
rules.plain_language: A bill is an order to pay; a promissory note is a promise to pay.
rules.scenario_relevance: The project mentions an L/C and related bill-of-exchange context, but no actual bill is supplied; do not presume that every L/C includes a bill.

rules.rule: A cheque is a bill of exchange drawn on a specified banker and not expressed to be payable otherwise than on demand.
rules.plain_language: A cheque is a bank-directed instrument payable on demand under its definition.
rules.scenario_relevance: The company cheque to a weaver reportedly bounced; the reason and presentation details are not given.

rules.rule: A negotiable instrument under the section means a promissory note, bill of exchange or cheque payable to order or bearer, subject to the Act's text.
rules.plain_language: The Act defines negotiable instruments through specified instruments; a Letter of Credit is not automatically one of them.
rules.scenario_relevance: Keep the L/C documentary payment arrangement distinct from any bill of exchange that may actually be drawn under it.

rules.rule: A promissory note, bill of exchange or cheque is dishonoured by non-payment when the maker, acceptor or drawee defaults on payment when duly required to pay.
rules.plain_language: Dishonour is assessed for the specific instrument and the payment demanded under it.
rules.scenario_relevance: The project refers to a bounced cheque and a promissory note coming due; handle them as separate instruments.

rules.topic: Dishonour of certain cheques for insufficiency of funds
rules.rule: Section 138 addresses specified cases where a cheque is returned unpaid for insufficient funds or exceeding an arrangement, subject to the section's statutory conditions and procedure.
rules.plain_language: A bounced cheque does not by itself establish every element or procedural condition of an offence under section 138.
rules.scenario_relevance: The project gives no cheque date, reason for return, notice or other procedural facts; avoid concluding that section 138 applies.
